package_info.why_malicious: Snake is a state-sponsored espionage malware developed by Russia’s FSB (Turla group) to covertly steal sensitive documents and maintain persistent, stealthy access to high-value targets worldwide. It forms a global P2P network of compromised systems for long-term intelligence collection.

execution_context.file_location: core Snake malware binary (varies by deployment)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Establishes encrypted peer-to-peer (P2P) communications with other infected hosts, relaying commands and exfiltrated data covertly.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C/C++ (typical for Snake, but exact language not specified)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes encrypted P2P connections with other infected systems, relays commands and exfiltrates sensitive data, enabling covert global espionage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: P2P encrypted communications between compromised hosts are highly unusual for legitimate software and are a hallmark of advanced persistent threats.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not create covert P2P networks for command and control or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some distributed computing or blockchain applications use P2P, but not for hidden, encrypted C2 or data theft.
key_indicators: Encrypted P2P traffic to non-standard ports

execution_context.file_location: core Snake malware binary (varies by deployment)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steals sensitive documents from infected systems and exfiltrates them via the P2P network.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C/C++ (typical for Snake, but exact language not specified)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code searches for and collects sensitive documents, then exfiltrates them through the encrypted P2P network to attacker-controlled nodes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated, covert collection and exfiltration of sensitive files is a core indicator of espionage malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently search for and transmit sensitive documents without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or sync tools may access files, but with user awareness and legitimate destinations.
key_indicators: Covert exfiltration via custom network protocol

execution_context.file_location: core Snake malware binary (varies by deployment)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Receives and executes self-destruct/overwrite commands, erasing its own vital components to disable itself.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C/C++ (typical for Snake, but exact language not specified)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On receiving a specific command, the code overwrites its own executable components, effectively disabling the malware without harming the host system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-destruct and anti-forensic capabilities are typical of advanced malware seeking to evade detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not erase itself in response to remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate uninstallers remove software, but not in response to covert network commands.

attack_chain.action: Initial infection and installation of Snake malware on target systems.
Establishes encrypted P2P communications with other infected hosts, forming a global network.
Searches for and collects sensitive documents from infected systems.
Exfiltrates stolen data via the encrypted P2P network to attacker-controlled nodes.
On command (e.g., from FBI’s PEGASUS tool), Snake overwrites its own components to self-destruct and disable itself.

behavioral_signatures: Encrypted P2P network traffic between internal and external hosts
Automated file system scanning and access to sensitive documents
Remote-triggered self-deletion or overwriting of executables
file_indicators: Unknown or suspicious binaries with persistence mechanisms
Unusual modification or deletion of malware-related files
Artifacts of custom P2P protocol handlers
network_indicators: Non-standard encrypted traffic to multiple peer hosts
Unusual outbound connections to known Snake/Turla infrastructure
Relay of data between internal and external nodes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for encrypted P2P traffic patterns, especially on non-standard ports; look for automated file access and exfiltration behaviors; detect binaries with self-modifying or self-deleting capabilities; correlate with known Turla/Snake infrastructure and threat intelligence feeds.
